findings.trigger_condition: Input contains many unhashable nodes or mixes hashable and unhashable nodes at scale, e.g. a deep chain of lists `(([i],[i-1]) for i in range(1,100000))`, or a graph with ~10^4-10^5 nodes of both kinds (str nodes + list nodes).
findings.root_cause: `_id_of` performs an unconditional linear scan for every lookup: the unhashable path scans ALL registered unhashable_ids (O(U)) and ALL hashable_ids (O(H)) per call (lines 64-72), and the hashable path scans ALL unhashable_ids per call (lines 83-87), with no canonicalization or bucketing of unhashable values (e.g. list->tuple, set->frozenset, bytearray->bytes). Total cost is O(U^2 + H*U), quadratic in the number of unhashable and mixed nodes, even when no cross-kind equality ever occurs.
findings.impact: Valid inputs promised by the contract ('Handle very deep acyclic inputs without recursion') take quadratic time and effectively hang at scale. Measured: 60k-node hashable chain = 0.10s, but 3k-node unhashable chain = 0.59s (~1200x more work per node) and 3k hashable + 3k unhashable mixed graph = 0.98s. A 10^5-node unhashable chain extrapolates to ~10+ minutes and a 10^5+10^5 mixed graph to ~20 minutes, so hidden scale tests time out.
findings.suggested_validation: Time `dependency_layers((([i],[i-1]) for i in range(1,100000)))` (expect near-linear, ~seconds; observe minutes) and a 50k hashable + 50k unhashable mixed graph. Fix: bucket canonicalized forms of common unhashable types (list->tuple, set->frozenset, bytearray->bytes, dict->frozenset of items) and restrict/eliminate the unconditional cross-kind full scans.

findings.trigger_condition: Node values are objects whose `__eq__` returns a non-bool truthy-ambiguous value, e.g. numpy arrays (unhashable, valid node objects per the list[list[object]] contract). Any input with two or more such nodes triggers it - the second array crashes even when the arrays are unequal, because `==` is evaluated for every candidate pair.
findings.root_cause: `_same_node` evaluates `left is right or left == right` (line 41) and relies on `==` yielding a plain bool. For numpy arrays `left == right` returns an element-wise ndarray and `bool(ndarray)` raises ValueError ('The truth value of an array with more than one element is ambiguous'), which propagates out of the equality scans (lines 65/69/79/84) uncaught.
findings.impact: `dependency_layers` crashes with an unrelated ValueError (not DependencyCycleError) on any input containing >=2 numpy-array (or similar pandas/object-dtype) nodes, even for a perfectly acyclic graph, instead of returning layers or a proper cycle error. Verified: both equal-array pairs and unequal-array pairs raise ValueError.
findings.suggested_validation: Run `dependency_layers([(np.array([1,2]), 'a'), (np.array([3,4]), 'b')])` - expect layered output, currently ValueError. Fix: `if left is right: return True` then `eq = left == right; return isinstance(eq, bool) and eq` (guard against non-bool `==` results) so exotic equality semantics degrade to 'not equal' instead of raising.
